topic_title: Top 9 Dog Breeds With Gorgeous Curly and Wavy Coats You’ll Love
intro: Curly and wavy coats look different and live differently. Tight curls, as on Poodles, Bichons and the Lagotto, trap loose hair inside the coat, so they shed little onto floors but mat quickly without brushing and need regular clipping. Wavy coats, as on spaniels and the Wheaten, shed more but are usually easier to maintain at home. Budget for grooming before choosing: a curly breed can cost more in trims each year than in food.

picks.description: The Sussex Spaniel is a low-slung, golden-liver spaniel with a long, wavy coat and a famously calm, easygoing nature. It has the lowest energy on this list, so daily walks of about 30 to 45 minutes are usually enough. The coat sheds moderately and needs brushing a few times a week. Sussex Spaniels weigh 35 to 45 pounds and are gentle, loyal and good with children and other pets. They can be slow to train and may bark or howl when they catch a scent. The breed is rare, so expect a breeder waitlist.
picks.best_for: Calm households wanting a relaxed spaniel with a wavy coat
picks.quirky_fact: Sussex Spaniels were bred to bark while hunting so hunters could follow them in dense cover.
picks.skip_if: You want a fast learner or an easy-to-find breed

picks.description: The Field Spaniel has a flat-to-wavy, glossy coat with feathering on the legs and chest. It sheds moderately and needs brushing a couple of times a week plus tidying around the feet and ears. Field Spaniels weigh 35 to 50 pounds and are calmer than many sporting breeds, though they still need around an hour of exercise a day. They are gentle, affectionate and good with children and other pets, and they can be sensitive, so soft handling works best. Like other spaniels, their ears need regular cleaning.
picks.best_for: Families wanting a calmer, gentle spaniel with a wavy coat
picks.quirky_fact: Field Spaniels nearly disappeared in the mid-1900s and were rebuilt by a small group of breeders.
picks.skip_if: You want a low-shedding dog or rarely have time for walks

picks.description: The American Water Spaniel is a rare, brown, curly-to-wavy coated hunting dog from the Great Lakes region. Its coat is oily and water-resistant, sheds moderately and needs weekly brushing and occasional trimming. At 25 to 45 pounds it is compact for a gundog, and it needs about an hour of exercise daily, with swimming as a favorite. AWS are friendly, smart and good with families and other pets, though some can be reserved with strangers. They do best with an active owner who enjoys the outdoors.
picks.best_for: Outdoorsy owners wanting a compact, curly-coated water dog
picks.quirky_fact: The American Water Spaniel is the state dog of Wisconsin.
picks.skip_if: You want a common breed with easy breeder access

picks.description: The Cocker Spaniel's coat is wavy and silky, with long feathering on the ears, chest and legs. It sheds moderately and needs brushing a few times a week plus a trim every six to eight weeks to keep feet and ears tidy. Cockers weigh 20 to 30 pounds and are affectionate, gentle and good with children and other pets. Energy is moderate, around 45 minutes of walks and play a day. Their long ears trap moisture and need weekly cleaning to prevent infections. Some Cockers can be sensitive to harsh handling, so gentle, reward-based training works best.
picks.best_for: Families wanting a gentle, medium dog with a classic wavy coat
picks.quirky_fact: The name comes from woodcock, the game bird these spaniels were bred to flush.
picks.skip_if: You won't keep up with ear cleaning and regular trims

picks.description: The Lagotto Romagnolo is an Italian water dog now best known for hunting truffles. Its dense, woolly curls shed little but need regular brushing and clipping every couple of months to prevent cording and mats. Lagottos weigh 24 to 35 pounds, have moderate energy and love work for their nose, so scent games and puzzle toys keep them content. They are affectionate, good with children and other pets, and fairly trainable, though some can be sensitive or vocal. At 14 to 16 years, they are one of the longer-lived breeds on this list.
picks.best_for: Owners wanting a medium, low-shedding curly dog that loves nose work
picks.quirky_fact: Lagottos are the only breed recognized specifically as a truffle-hunting dog.
picks.skip_if: You won't commit to regular clipping or mental exercise

picks.description: The Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier has a silky, gently wavy wheat-colored coat rather than tight curls. It sheds less than most medium dogs but tangles easily, so plan on brushing several times a week and a trim every couple of months. Wheatens weigh 30 to 40 pounds and are friendly, bouncy and good with children and other pets. They need about an hour of exercise a day and are known for an exuberant jumping greeting, the Wheaten greetin', which takes training to manage. They can be moderately stubborn, so short, positive sessions work best.
picks.best_for: Active families wanting a friendly, medium dog with a soft wavy coat
picks.quirky_fact: Wheaten puppies are born dark and their coats lighten to the wheat color over the first couple of years.
picks.skip_if: You want a calm greeter or won't brush several times a week

picks.description: The Miniature Poodle, around 10 to 15 pounds, has the same dense curly coat as other Poodles with a sturdier build than the Toy, which makes it a good middle ground for families. The coat sheds little but needs regular brushing and a professional trim every four to eight weeks. Energy is high: an hour of walks, play and training each day keeps it calm indoors. Minis are intelligent, eager learners that excel at tricks and dog sports, and they get along with children and other pets. Without enough activity they can become noisy or anxious.
picks.best_for: Active households wanting a small, sturdy, low-shedding curly dog
picks.quirky_fact: Poodle curls keep growing like human hair, which is why they need clipping instead of shedding seasonally.
picks.skip_if: You want a low-energy dog or can't budget for regular grooming

picks.description: The Toy Poodle packs the Poodle's tight, low-shedding curls into a dog of 4 to 6 pounds. Its coat needs daily brushing and a trim every four to six weeks, and clips can be kept short and practical. Despite its size, energy is high and the breed is very intelligent, so it needs daily walks plus training games or puzzle toys to stay settled. Toy Poodles are affectionate and easy to train, and they get along with other pets. Their small size makes them fragile around rough play, so they fit best with adults or older children. Some bark readily, which training can reduce.
picks.best_for: Adults wanting a tiny, clever, low-shedding curly dog
picks.quirky_fact: Poodles of all sizes regularly rank among the easiest breeds to train.
picks.skip_if: You have toddlers or can't provide daily mental exercise

picks.description: The Bichon Frise has a soft, dense curly coat that gives it its powder-puff look and sheds very little onto floors. That coat is also the main commitment: brush most days to prevent mats and book a professional groom every four to six weeks. At 12 to 18 pounds, Bichons suit apartments, and their energy is moderate, around 30 to 45 minutes of play and walks a day. They are cheerful, easy to train and good with children, cats and other dogs. Expect some barking at the door and a tendency to dislike being alone for long hours. House-training can take longer than average, so consistency matters.
picks.best_for: Apartment dwellers wanting a cheerful, low-shedding curly companion
picks.quirky_fact: Bichons often do a sudden burst of zooming around the room, which owners call the Bichon blitz.
picks.skip_if: You won't brush most days or pay for regular professional grooming

faqs.question: Which dog breeds have curly hair?
faqs.answer: Breeds with tightly curled coats include the Poodle in all three sizes, the Bichon Frise, the Lagotto Romagnolo, the Portuguese Water Dog, the Irish Water Spaniel, the Curly-Coated Retriever and the American Water Spaniel. Many doodle crosses also have curly coats, though texture varies from puppy to puppy.

faqs.question: Do curly-haired dogs shed less?
faqs.answer: Usually. Tight curls catch loose hair before it falls, so curly breeds leave far less hair on furniture. That hair still needs to be brushed out, or it forms mats close to the skin. Wavy-coated breeds like spaniels shed noticeably more.

faqs.question: Are curly-coated dogs hypoallergenic?
faqs.answer: No dog is truly hypoallergenic, because allergens come from dander, saliva and urine as well as hair. Low-shedding curly breeds spread less hair and dander around the home, which some allergy sufferers tolerate better. Spend time with the breed before committing.

faqs.question: How often do curly-coated dogs need grooming?
faqs.answer: Tightly curled breeds such as Poodles and Bichons need brushing most days and a professional trim every four to eight weeks. Wavy breeds like Cocker and Field Spaniels need brushing a few times a week and an occasional tidy, especially around the ears and feet.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a curly and a wavy coat?
faqs.answer: A curly coat forms tight ringlets or a dense, springy texture that holds loose hair inside it. A wavy coat has loose waves, often with longer feathering on ears, legs and belly. Wavy coats shed more but are usually less prone to dense matting.

seo_title: 9 Curly and Wavy Coated Dog Breeds (2026 Guide)
answer: The Bichon Frise, Toy Poodle and Miniature Poodle have the tightest curls and shed the least of any breeds here. For a wavy coat with less grooming, look at the Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier, Cocker Spaniel or Field Spaniel. The deciding factor is grooming: tight curls mean daily brushing and a professional trim every four to eight weeks.
method: We filtered a 150-breed dataset for breeds whose coat is described as curly or wavy, then ordered them from tightest curl and lowest shedding to looser waves, noting grooming, energy and temperament for each.
